resultsDay.title: Results day
resultsDay.intro: What your marks mean and what to do next. Ticks stay in this browser.

steps.title: Read your results on the UoL portal
steps.hint: Each course has a mark out of 100: 70 and above is first class, 60 to 69 upper second, 50 to 59 lower second, 40 to 49 third, and under 40 a fail.

steps.title: Under 40 is a fail, not the end
steps.hint: You get up to three attempts at each course, and the most recent mark counts. The degree needs passes in at least 330 of its 360 credits, including every core course (regulations 5.11, 8.5 and 8.6).

links.label: Try it in the grades calculator

steps.title: Enter for your resit before the exam entry deadline
steps.hint: You enter a resit on the UoL portal, like any exam. A session where you take a new course must also include any failed course that is compulsory or a prerequisite for it (regulation 5.13).

steps.title: Think a mark is wrong? Ask for a recheck
steps.hint: The University can check that every answer was marked and the marks were added up and recorded correctly. It doesn’t re-mark for academic judgement. There’s a fee and a deadline a few weeks after results day: its results page gives both.

steps.title: Talk it through with someone at BIBF
steps.hint: Your student reps and BIBF’s programme team can help you plan resits and next year’s modules. Bring your marks.

steps.title: Plan the year ahead
steps.hint: Put your marks in the grades calculator to see your class so far and what each course still to come needs.
